links.comparator_used: Default raw FHIR JSON serialisation (raw_json) versus five other FHIR-to-text formats, including structured_markdown and hybrid_adaptive
links.outcome: Clinical LLM quality (scored 1-5) across clinical QA, clinical reasoning and summarisation tasks
links.effect: Format choice significantly affected quality (Kruskal-Wallis H=163.86, p<10^-33, Δ=0.24 on a 5-point scale). raw_json was suboptimal in 58% of model-task-complexity scenarios. raw_json was best for clinical QA, hybrid_adaptive for clinical reasoning, and structured_markdown for summarisation. Format sensitivity was 0.10 points for Claude Sonnet 4.5 versus 0.39 for Llama 3.3.
links.quote: The optimal format is context-dependent: raw_json dominates for clinical QA, hybrid_adaptive for clinical reasoning, and structured_markdown for summarisation.
